Please find below a comparative analysis of AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) and NVDA (NVIDIA Corporation) as of market open, December 1, 2025. This report covers current valuations, key metrics, recent developments, and investment risks for both high-performance computing chip leaders.

================================================================================
CURRENT PRICES & KEY VALUATION METRICS
================================================================================

AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.)
  • Current Price: $219.56
  • Market Cap (Intraday): $327B
  • EPS (TTM): $1.91
  • PE Ratio (TTM): 105.27
  • 52-Week Range: $76.48 – $267.08
  • Beta (5Y Monthly): 1.93
  • 1-Year Target Estimate: $281.47
  • Volume: 17,179,364

NVDA (NVIDIA Corporation)
  • Current Price: $179.09
  • Market Cap (Intraday): $4,240B
  • EPS (TTM): $4.04
  • PE Ratio (TTM): 43.10
  • 52-Week Range: $86.62 – $212.19
  • Beta (5Y Monthly): 2.28
  • 1-Year Target Estimate: $252.67
  • Volume: 94,249,614
  • Forward Dividend Yield: 0.02%
  • Ex-Dividend Date: Dec 04, 2025

================================================================================
VALUATION COMPARISON
================================================================================

Relative Valuation:
  • NVIDIA trades at a significantly more attractive P/E of 43.10x vs AMD's 105.27x,
    despite NVIDIA's massive $4.24T market cap. This reflects NVIDIA's superior earnings
    power with EPS of $4.04 per share (TTM).
  • AMD's $327B market cap is roughly 1/13th of NVIDIA's, yet its P/E is more than
    double, suggesting the market is pricing in higher future growth expectations
    for AMD's competitive positioning.
  • On an absolute basis, both stocks trade well below their 1-year analyst targets
    (AMD: $281.47 / $219.56 = 128% vs target; NVDA: $252.67 / $179.09 = 141% vs target).

EPS Strength:
  • NVIDIA's EPS of $4.04 (TTM) significantly outpaces AMD's $1.91, reflecting NVIDIA's
    dominant position in AI accelerators and data center GPUs.
  • NVIDIA's lower P/E combined with higher EPS provides a more compelling earnings yield.

================================================================================
BROADER MARKET CONTEXT
================================================================================

Today's Market Overview (December 1, 2025):
  • NASDAQ: 15,005.53 (+0.55, +0.06%)
  • S&P 500: 14,966.10 (-3.39, -0.34%)
  • DOW: 14,977.37 (-2.26, -0.23%)

Trending Movers:
  • #1 Trending: NVDA at $179.09 (+1.19%)
  • #8 Trending: AMD at $219.56 (+0.93%)

Both semiconductor names are among today's most-ticked stocks, indicating sustained
investor interest. NVIDIA's top trending position reflects continued market enthusiasm
for AI infrastructure plays.

================================================================================
RECENT NEWS & DEVELOPMENTS
================================================================================

AMD Developments:
  1. Bank of Maintain Buy Rating – "Competition Is Heating Up, But Bank of America
     Still Thinks AMD Stock Is a Buy Here" (Dec 1, 2025). BofA remains confident in
     AMD's AI chip future despite intensifying competition from NVIDIA and others.
  2. Ryzen Product Listing – "Official Ryzen Listing Ignites High-Performance CPU Hype"
     suggesting renewed interest in AMD's desktop/server CPU portfolio.
  3. AMD Stock Drops 15% in a Month – raising questions about near-term entry points.

NVDA Developments:
  1. NVIDIA Invests $2B in Synopsys – "Nvidia Invests $2 Billion in Synopsys to Broaden
     AI Design Partnership" (Dec 1, 2025), signaling deepening software/EDA ecosystem
     integration and strategic moat-building.
  2. Nvidia Stock Bounces Back – Benzinga coverage highlights recovery momentum after
     recent weakness.
  3. Meta TPU Competition – "Meta Might Use Google TPUs in 2027. Should Nvidia Investors
     Panic?" – addressing long-term customer diversification risks.

================================================================================
RELATIVE STRENGTHS
================================================================================

NVIDIA's Strengths:
  • Dominant AI accelerator market position with industry-leading Hopper/Blackwell GPUs
  • Superior earnings generation: EPS of $4.04 vs AMD's $1.91
  • Attractive valuation: P/E of 43.10x vs AMD's 105.27x despite larger market cap
  • $4.24T market cap demonstrates scale, platform credibility, and investor confidence
  • Expanding ecosystem through Synopsys $2B investment
  • Higher analyst upside: 41% vs target price

AMD's Strengths:
  • Competitive CPU portfolio (EPYC, Ryzen) in data center and consumer markets
  • Developing MI300 AI accelerators to challenge NVIDIA's GPU dominance
  • Lower absolute stock price may attract retail/retail-oriented investors
  • Bank of America bullish outlook provides near-term support
  • More diversified revenue streams (PCs, servers, embedded)

================================================================================
KEY RISKS
================================================================================

NVIDIA Risks:
  • Competition from AMD (MI300), Intel (Gaudi), and custom AI chips from hyperscalers
  • Potential customer concentration – large hyperscalers may develop in-house alternatives
  • High beta (2.28) amplifies market volatility
  • Stock down ~15% from highs; near-term weakness possible
  • Regulatory/geopolitical risks (China export restrictions)

AMD Risks:
  • Extremely high P/E of 105.27x implies significant execution pressure
  • NVIDIA's technological and ecosystem lead is substantial and difficult to close
  • 52-week low of $76.48 demonstrates severe past volatility
  • Declining 15% over the past month suggests near-term momentum challenges
  • Lower EPS ($1.91) compared to NVIDIA limits earnings-based upside

================================================================================
CONCLUSION
================================================================================

Both AMD and NVIDIA represent compelling but distinct investment profiles in the
high-performance computing sector.

NVIDIA offers superior earnings fundamentals ($4.04 EPS vs $1.91), a more attractive
P/E valuation (43.10x vs 105.27x), and dominant AI market positioning, but carries
concentration and competition risks at its $4.24T market cap. The stock's recent pullback
from $212.19 to $179.09 (with a 52-week low of $86.62) presents a potential entry point
for long-term AI infrastructure exposure.

AMD, at $219.56 with a $327B market cap, offers a competitive play on CPU and emerging
AI accelerator markets. The stock has declined sharply (52-week low: $76.48) and faces
a steep valuation challenge at 105.27x P/E. The Bank of America buy rating provides
near-term sentiment support, but execution on MI300 adoption will be critical.

Recommendation: For conservative exposure to AI infrastructure, NVIDIA's earnings power
and valuation justify a premium positioning. For tactical opportunity in a competitive
challenger with catalyst potential, AMD warrants monitoring around current levels.

---
This analysis is based on market data as of December 1, 2025, 1:30 PM ET. All figures
cited are from live stock page data. This report is for informational purposes only
and does not constitute investment advice.

Regards,
Chipmaker Analytics
